rows.subtopic: Integrity vs despair (as foreseen by the young)
rows.description: A young person hears a grandparent say they wish they had studied or spoken up. They take it as a warning not a burden, and think about which risks now are worth their future self's peace.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Integrity vs despair (as foreseen by the young)
rows.subtype: Living so the story is one you can accept [Response]
rows.description: A young professional considers what they want to be able to say in old age and lets it shape ordinary choices: keeping promises, repairing rifts, doing work that matters. They accept that no life is regret-free.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtopic: Integrity vs despair (as foreseen by the young)
rows.description: A young adult sees an older relative who dwells on old grievances and unfinished ambitions. They feel compassion and a resolve not to end up rehearsing resentments, while still listening without lecturing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: grief, resentment, determination, empathy

rows.description: A child loves showing a younger sibling how to tie shoes or draw, feeling proud to be the one who knows. This early urge to pass something on is the seed of later generativity.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager tutors younger students or helps organise a neighbourhood cleanup and feels needed. Being useful to others gives a sense of worth that grades and status do not.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult volunteers, mentors school kids or builds a small project not for credit but because they want their effort to outlast them. It sits alongside ambition, not in place of it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young worker settles into a routine, thinks only of salary and comfort, and feels flat when asked what they are building. It is not laziness; it is a life turned entirely inward.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young professional shares what they learned with a junior, credits them publicly and accepts being outgrown. Generativity means caring for what grows, not owning it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult in their early twenties feels neither like a child nor fully an adult: financially partly dependent, making choices alone, unsure whether to say they have grown up. The feeling is common and not a failure.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.description: A graduate sees many possible careers, cities and partners and feels both excitement and dread of choosing wrongly. The openness is a gift, but it can freeze decisions or invite endless comparison.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
